format.summary: The hosts call Reality Fracture a highly synergistic, high-power, well-designed set built around Empower Jace (put loyalty on or create a Jace token with -3 draw a card and -1 surveil 1), plus prepare creatures sharing prepare spells, threshold, and flashback. Ten supported two-color archetypes split into five allied schools and five enemy planeswalker pairs, with many hybrid cards overlapping across decks. Marshall predicted the set will end up graded A- or better.
format.speed: Not directly measured, but they said games tend to be fast (bounce is good), Jace tokens make attacking and trample important, and limited rewards high-roll starts like turn-two Ways.

colors.take: Deep in life gain, +1/+1 counters, and legends, with solid removal like Your Fate Ends Here and Memory Trap.
Surveil, card draw, and Jace-empowering commons like Mindseeker Oculus, with better-than-usual removal for blue.
Very removal-rich (Last Gasp, Multiply by Zero, Break Under Pressure, Extended Absence) with self-mill and threshold support.
Lots of efficient burn (No Admittance, Wrath of the Bloodmane, Violent Echoes, Fulminous Forte), non-combat pings, and strong landcyclers.
Ramp via Heartwood tokens and mana creatures, fight/bite removal, and big top end like Ghalta.

pairs.take: Fatehold surveil aggro; signposts like Fatehold Charm and Desperate Futurescribe look strong.
Theorix self-mill to threshold (seven cards in the graveyard); Luis loves the Paradox Shaper loop and Recursive Recruitment.
Stingerquill non-combat face-damage payoffs; enablers like Voxmancer and Stingerquill Charm make it look scary.
Konstrari ramp using Heartwood mana tokens into big payoffs like Craftwork Crusher; the charm and improviser are weak, and the payoff quality determines viability.
Vigorbloom life gain and counters, heavily supported with busted Bloombrute and strong common enablers.
Liliana's small recursive creatures and graveyard grind, overlapping with the life-gain cards; Twisted Fates is a standout.
Chandra's prowess and noncreature spells; Saheeli and Clash of Elements are strong, but they are wary of prowess as a primary plan.
Garruk's deathtouch-plus-trample theme; Hapatra and Primal Witchstalker are strong, but the theme needs to prove itself.
Ajani's aggressive +1/+1 counters deck with Mabel and Warrior's Blades.
Jace's mastery: repeatedly empowering Jace for card flow and converting loyalty into board presence via Kiora, Ways, and Compel Brutality; potentially fragile.

mechanics.name: Empower Jace
mechanics.take: Intuitive, creative, and everywhere; it adds decisions about using or attacking Jaces, and Empower 4 is the sweet spot for an immediate card while leaving Jace behind.

mechanics.name: Prepare
mechanics.take: Kept simple by sharing the same prepare spell within each color pair (Peer Review, Omit Variables, Vicious Verse, Soul Tether, Seed Suture), which reduces cognitive load.

mechanics.name: Heartwood tokens
mechanics.take: Red-green mana-rock tokens; they are skeptical that three-mana ramp is worth it unless payoffs like Craftwork Crusher show up.

mechanics.name: Threshold
mechanics.take: Blue-black payoffs for having seven or more cards in the graveyard, well supported by self-mill.

mechanics.name: Ways (legendary enchantments)
mechanics.take: Cheap Ways are wheel-spinning build-arounds, while the more expensive Ways (Wildspeaker, Healer, Warlord, Mind Sculptor) are strong and grant abilities to all future Jaces.

mechanics.name: Basic landcycling
mechanics.take: A common cycle at five-plus mana that is unusually strong, which they say makes formats more fun.

mechanics.name: Color hosers
mechanics.take: A cycle of cheap hoser removal and counters that are sideboard B's in best-of-three and should not be played in best-of-one.

advice: Play your spells before combat against possible Countersculpt so you can attack the resulting Jace if they counter.
Decide actively whether to attack, burn, or ignore opposing Jaces; trample, deathtouch-trample, and evasive creatures are valuable for killing them.
Cheap removal that trades up on mana is premium in a format full of strong three- to five-drops.
Don't overload on card-draw spells since most cards already generate Jace value; keep enough action.
Sideboard color hosers only in best-of-three; skip them in best-of-one.
Value hybrid cards and cross-archetype enablers such as Blessed Ghoul and life-gain triggers, since they fit several decks.
Annex dual lands go up in value when you already have enough playables.
Optimize for strong early starts, since high rolls like turn-two Way of the Pyromancer are how limited is won.
